text:
Marta: Heads up — noticed a short spike on dedicated-eu-rt-pool around 11:12 UTC, apps saw 503s. Can someone point me to the best place to pull traces/logs for that pool? I can see metrics in Grafana but want raw logs.

Leo: Did you check `pool_saturation` and `autoscaler_replicas`? Dashboard link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/pools/dedicated-capacity?orgId=1&var-pool=eu-rt-pool — that shows per-pool histograms.

Marta: I did, saturation hit ~0.92 for ~3min. Need traces and request IDs to tie to client errors.

Tanvi: For logs, use Loki: https://logs.redwood.internal/logql. Quick LogQL snippet that helped me:
```
{pool="eu-rt-pool"} |= "start req" |~ "request_id|trace_id"
```
We tag traces with `x-rw-trace` header, so search for that too.

Josh: For traces go to Tempo: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/<trace_id> or search by service `serving-runtime` + pool label. If you have `req=...` sometimes the trace_id is in the request log line.

Leo: FYI alert `pool_high_saturation` fired but auto-resolved quickly. We should consider changing to a 5m avg and adding suppression when replicas are ramping. Current PromQL is basically:
```
avg_over_time(pool_saturation[1m]) > 0.85
```
Proposal: evaluate `avg_over_time(pool_saturation[5m]) > 0.85` and gate it with a stability check (eg. no replica changes in the last 5m).

Marta: Can we tune to ignore transient spikes from rollout/scale events? Those cause noisy paging and aren't helpful.

Tanvi: Yes — we can add a `replica_change_in_last_5m` condition or require sustained 3m above threshold after the autoscaler is stable. Ops-bot has a helper to annotate suppression windows.

ops-bot: To add suppression, submit PR to `infra/monitoring/alerts` with annotation `suppress_during_scaling: true` and include selector `pool =~ "^eu-"` if you only want EU pools. See docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/monitoring#suppressions

Josh: I've opened PR #3822 with new rule `pool_high_saturation_v2` that uses 5m avg and a suppression window: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/3822 — reviewers: @Tanvi @Marta.

Marta: Thanks — can someone paste a sample request_id or trace so I can correlate? I saw this in logs: `req=8a4f2c trace=7b9d1` but search returns nothing.

Tanvi: Try escaping special chars and do a regex search. Example LogQL: `|~ "trace=([0-9a-f]+)"`. I found `trace=7b9d1f2c3a` at 2026-02-12T11:12:07Z. Trace view: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/7b9d1f2c3a

Leo: I looked at the trace — root span shows a `kv_cache_miss` storm, KV miss rate jumped from ~0.05 to ~0.6 for that pool during the spike. That correlated with a downstream latency increase. We should emit `kv_cache_miss_rate` per-pool.

Tanvi: Filing issue ENG-1159 to add `kv_cache_miss_rate` and tag it by `pool` + `model_type`: https://issues.redwood.internal/ENG-1159 — will add a 1m and 5m series.

Marta: Great. For the alert tuning, if the PR merges, can someone schedule a quiet window to observe? I'd like to run a small load test to reproduce and verify the alert behavior.

Josh: I'll coordinate a canary on staging tomorrow 09:00 PT and tag this thread with results. Assigning @Marta and @Tanvi for validation.

Marta: ack, thanks everyone.

ops-bot: Reminder: after PR merge, infra will auto-deploy alert rules at next roll. If you need manual rollout, ping #eng-infra.
